text: Inside this giant wooden horse outside Troy, thirty Greek soldiers were sealed alive in thirty-five-degree heat. The hollow pine belly held two cramped tiers where warriors sat in absolute silence.
At midnight, Odysseus unlocked a spring-loaded trapdoor beneath the horse, dropping hemp ropes to the cobblestones below.
They slipped into the city, opened the gates, and ended a ten-year siege in a single night. Subscribe to IR in a Nutshell.
